ideas.title: Add skeleton loading states for data tables
ideas.description: Implement skeleton placeholder loading states that match the layout of data tables during HTMX requests and page loads
ideas.rationale: Currently, data tables show no visual feedback during loading except a small spinner. Skeleton screens reduce perceived load time and prevent layout shifts, improving user experience during navigation and filtering
ideas.current_state: When filtering/paginating tables via HTMX, users see either nothing or a small spinner. The table content disappears briefly, causing layout shift.
ideas.proposed_change: Create a new _table_skeleton.html component with Tabler's placeholder-glow animation. Apply skeleton states during hx-request class. Example: Add '.htmx-request .table tbody { display: none; } .htmx-request .table-skeleton { display: block; }' pattern with 5-row skeleton placeholder showing loading animation for each column.
ideas.user_benefit: Users see a meaningful loading state that matches the expected content layout, reducing confusion about whether the app is responding and preventing jarring content jumps

ideas.title: Enhance keyboard accessibility for modal dialogs
ideas.description: Add proper focus trapping, focus restoration, and keyboard navigation to all Alpine.js modals
ideas.rationale: Current modals (like the movement modal in stock_list.html) lack focus trapping - users can tab out of the modal while it's open. This is both an accessibility issue (WCAG 2.1 Level A) and a usability problem
ideas.current_state: Modals open without moving focus to the modal content. Tab key allows focus to escape to elements behind the modal overlay. No focus restoration when modal closes. Escape key works but isn't consistently implemented.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Update Alpine.js modal data function in app.js to include focusTrap logic: store previous active element on open, set focus to first focusable element in modal, trap Tab/Shift+Tab within modal bounds, restore focus on close. 2. Add aria-modal='true' and role='dialog' attributes to modal containers. 3. Add aria-hidden='true' to .page wrapper when modal is open. Example: x-init="$el.querySelectorAll('button, input, select, textarea')[0]?.focus()" on modal open.
ideas.user_benefit: Keyboard-only users and screen reader users can navigate modals correctly. Focus returns to the trigger button after closing, maintaining navigation context

ideas.title: Add search input debouncing with visual feedback
ideas.description: Implement debounced search with a visual typing indicator for all search/filter forms
ideas.rationale: Search forms like in material_list.html trigger on form submit, requiring manual button clicks. For better UX, debounced auto-search with visual feedback would reduce friction. The debounce function exists in app.js but isn't being used.
ideas.current_state: Search inputs require clicking the 'Filtrar' button or pressing Enter. No auto-search functionality. No visual indication that typing will trigger a search after a delay.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Add hx-trigger='keyup changed delay:400ms' to search inputs for debounced search. 2. Add a typing indicator CSS class that shows '...' or a subtle pulse animation when user is typing. 3. Update search input pattern: <input type='text' name='search' class='form-control' hx-get='...' hx-trigger='keyup changed delay:400ms, search' hx-target='#results' hx-indicator='#search-indicator'>. 4. Add CSS: '.search-typing::after { content: "..."; animation: pulse 1s infinite; }'
ideas.user_benefit: Users get instant feedback as they type, reducing clicks needed to search. Visual indicator shows the system is responding to their input, improving perceived responsiveness

ideas.title: Add ARIA labels to icon-only action buttons
ideas.description: Add descriptive aria-label attributes to all icon-only buttons and links in data tables and navigation
ideas.rationale: Action buttons in tables (view, edit, delete) use only icons without text or aria-labels. Screen readers announce these as 'button' or 'link' without context, making the interface inaccessible to visually impaired users
ideas.current_state: Icon buttons like <a href='...' class='btn btn-icon btn-sm btn-primary' title='Ver Detalhes'> lack aria-label. The title attribute provides hover tooltips but is not announced by screen readers by default.
ideas.proposed_change: Add aria-label matching the title to all icon-only buttons. Example: <a href='{% url "materials:detail" material.id %}' class='btn btn-icon btn-sm btn-primary' title='Ver Detalhes' aria-label='Ver detalhes do material {{ material.code }}'> For the sidebar toggle: add aria-label='Abrir menu de navegacao' and aria-expanded state. For pagination: aria-label='Pagina {{ num }}' and aria-current='page' for active page.
ideas.user_benefit: Screen reader users hear meaningful descriptions like 'Ver detalhes do material AL7075' instead of just 'link'. Complies with WCAG 2.1 Level A Success Criterion 1.1.1 (Non-text Content)

ideas.title: Add autofocus and enhanced form field interactions
ideas.description: Auto-focus the primary input field on form pages and add subtle interaction enhancements to form inputs
ideas.rationale: Forms like material_form.html don't focus the first input field on load, requiring users to manually click or tab to start typing. This adds unnecessary friction to data entry workflows.
ideas.current_state: Form pages load without focusing any input. Users must click the first field to begin typing. The login page has 'autocomplete=off' which hinders password managers. Search inputs don't have autofocus.
ideas.proposed_change: 1. Add autofocus attribute to primary input: <input type='text' name='code' id='...' autofocus ...>. 2. Remove 'autocomplete=off' from login form and use 'autocomplete=username'/'autocomplete=current-password' (already correct in login.html but form tag has autocomplete=off). 3. Add focus-visible ring styling for better keyboard navigation visibility: '.form-control:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--tblr-primary); outline-offset: 2px; }'. 4. For modals, use x-init to focus first input when opened.
ideas.user_benefit: Users can immediately start typing without clicking. Keyboard users see clear focus indicators. Password managers work correctly on the login page. Data entry is faster and more efficient

ideas.title: Fix N+1 Query in Material Search API
ideas.description: The `material_search_api()` endpoint iterates through materials and calls `material.get_best_price()` for each one, triggering a separate database query per material. This creates an N+1 query pattern where 10 search results generate 11 queries (1 main + 10 per-material).
ideas.rationale: This API endpoint is called on every keystroke for material autocomplete searches. With typical usage patterns of 2-3 searches per form interaction, this could generate 30+ database queries per user action. The fix is straightforward with `Prefetch` and annotation.
ideas.currentMetric: N+1 queries: 11 queries for 10 results, ~100ms response time under load
ideas.expectedImprovement: Single query with annotation, reduce to 1 query, ~10ms response time
ideas.implementation:
1. Use Django's annotate() with Min() to get best price in the main query
2. Replace: `materials = Material.objects.filter(...)` with `materials = Material.objects.filter(...).annotate(best_price=Min('materialsupplier__price_per_kg', filter=Q(materialsupplier__supplier__is_active=True)))`
3. Access `material.best_price` instead of calling `material.get_best_price()`
ideas.tradeoffs: Slight increase in main query complexity, but net reduction in total query time

ideas.title: Add Redis Caching for Dashboard Statistics
ideas.description: Dashboard views (materials/dashboard, inventory/dashboard, production stats) compute aggregate statistics on every page load using COUNT, SUM, and other aggregations. These queries run on potentially large tables without any caching.
ideas.rationale: Redis is already configured in docker-compose but not utilized in Django. Dashboard statistics rarely change and are perfect candidates for caching. Multiple users viewing dashboards amplify the database load unnecessarily.
ideas.currentMetric: 6-8 aggregate queries per dashboard load, ~200-400ms per request
ideas.expectedImprovement: 0 queries for cached requests, ~5ms cache lookup, 95%+ cache hit rate
ideas.implementation:
1. Add Django cache configuration for Redis in settings.py
2. Import cache: `from django.core.cache import cache`
3. Wrap stats computation: `stats = cache.get('dashboard_stats') or compute_and_cache()`
4. Set 60-second TTL for stats
5. Invalidate cache on relevant model signals (post_save, post_delete)
ideas.tradeoffs: Stats may be up to 60 seconds stale; requires cache invalidation strategy

ideas.title: Remove Unused Static File Plugins to Reduce Deployment Size
ideas.description: The staticfiles/plugins directory contains ~50MB of unused JavaScript libraries (DataTables extensions, CKEditor, Flot charts, etc.) that were likely part of an admin template. The actual application only uses Tabler, HTMX, and Alpine.js which are in static/vendor/.
ideas.rationale: Large static file directories slow down `collectstatic`, increase deployment image size, and waste storage. The unused plugins also pose security risks if they contain outdated vulnerable code. The base template confirms only Tabler/HTMX/Alpine are loaded.
ideas.currentMetric: ~50MB of static files, ~30 unused JavaScript plugins
ideas.expectedImprovement: ~45MB reduction, faster deployments, smaller Docker images
ideas.implementation:
1. Audit staticfiles/ vs static/ to confirm which are used
2. Create backup of staticfiles/plugins/
3. Remove unused plugins: DataTables, CKEditor, Flot, Morris charts, etc.
4. Remove legacy IE compatibility files (html5shiv, respond.js, excanvas)
5. Remove *.demo.min.js files
6. Run collectstatic to verify no missing assets
ideas.tradeoffs: Need to verify no templates reference these files before removal

ideas.title: Add Database Indexes for Frequently Filtered Fields
ideas.description: Several Django models filter on fields that lack explicit database indexes. Fields like `status`, `movement_type`, `is_active`, and date fields are used in WHERE clauses and ordering but rely on implicit indexing or full table scans.
ideas.rationale: List views filter by status (DRAFT, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED), movement_type (IN, OUT, TRANSFER), and date ranges. As data grows, these queries will become slower without proper indexes. PostgreSQL's query planner needs hints for optimal paths.
ideas.currentMetric: Sequential scans on status/type filters with large datasets
ideas.expectedImprovement: Index-only scans, 10-100x faster filtering on 10k+ records
ideas.implementation:
1. Add db_index=True to frequently filtered fields:
   - ProductionOrder.status
   - Batch.status
   - StockMovement.movement_type
   - StockMovement.created_at
   - InventoryCount.status
2. Create migration with `python manage.py makemigrations`
3. Apply migration with `python manage.py migrate`
4. Consider composite indexes for common filter combinations
ideas.tradeoffs: Indexes add write overhead and storage; only add for truly hot paths

ideas.title: Avoid Duplicate .count() Queries in List Views
ideas.description: List views like `material_list()`, `supplier_list()`, and `stock_list()` call `.count()` on filtered querysets and also pass the same queryset to Paginator. Django's Paginator internally calls `.count()` again, resulting in duplicate COUNT queries.
ideas.rationale: Each duplicate COUNT query adds 50-100ms on large tables. This pattern appears in at least 5 list views. The fix is simple: use paginator.count instead of calling queryset.count() separately.
ideas.currentMetric: 2 COUNT queries per list page load instead of 1
ideas.expectedImprovement: 50% reduction in COUNT queries, ~50ms saved per page load
ideas.implementation:
1. Remove standalone `.count()` calls like `'total_materials': materials.count()`
2. Use paginator properties instead:
   ```python
   paginator = Paginator(materials, 20)
   page_obj = paginator.get_page(page_number)
   # Instead of materials.count(), use:
   context['total_materials'] = paginator.count
   ```
3. Apply pattern across all list views
ideas.tradeoffs: None - purely beneficial change with no downsides

ideas.title: Split large inventory views.py into domain-specific modules
ideas.description: The file apps/inventory/views.py has grown to 1251 lines and handles multiple unrelated concerns: stock management, movements, warehouses, reservations, and inventory counts. This violates single responsibility and makes the code hard to navigate, test, and maintain.
ideas.rationale: Very large files increase cognitive load, make code reviews harder, and often lead to merge conflicts. The inventory app handles 5 distinct domains (stocks, movements, warehouses, reservations, counts) that each deserve their own view module. Smaller, focused modules are easier to test, maintain, and reason about.
ideas.currentState: Single 1251-line file containing 30+ view functions handling stocks, movements, warehouses, reservations, and inventory counts
ideas.proposedChange:
Split into domain-specific view modules:
- apps/inventory/views/__init__.py (re-exports)
- apps/inventory/views/dashboard.py (dashboard view)
- apps/inventory/views/stocks.py (stock_list, stock_detail)
- apps/inventory/views/movements.py (movements_list, create_movement)
- apps/inventory/views/warehouses.py (warehouse_list, warehouse_detail, warehouse_create, warehouse_update)
- apps/inventory/views/reservations.py (reservations_list, reservation_create, etc.)
- apps/inventory/views/counts.py (inventory_count_list, inventory_count_create, etc.)
ideas.codeExample:
# Current structure:
# apps/inventory/views.py (1251 lines, all domains mixed)

# Proposed structure:
# apps/inventory/views/__init__.py
from .dashboard import dashboard
from .stocks import stock_list, stock_detail
from .movements import movements_list, create_movement
from .warehouses import warehouse_list, warehouse_detail, warehouse_create, warehouse_update
from .reservations import reservations_list, reservation_create
from .counts import inventory_count_list, inventory_count_create
ideas.bestPractice: Single Responsibility Principle - each module should have one reason to change. Django best practice is to organize views by domain/resource when they grow beyond ~300 lines.
prerequisites: Ensure test coverage for inventory views before refactoring

ideas.title: Add tests for production and purchasing apps
ideas.description: The production (869 lines in views.py) and purchasing (1084 lines in views.py) apps have no test files, while other apps like inventory, materials, and accounts have comprehensive test coverage. This leaves critical business logic untested.
ideas.rationale: Production orders and purchasing workflows are core business functionality that should have thorough test coverage. Without tests, refactoring becomes risky, bugs may go undetected, and there's no documentation of expected behavior. The existing test patterns in apps/inventory/tests.py and apps/materials/tests.py can serve as templates.
ideas.currentState:
No test files exist in apps/production/ or apps/purchasing/ directories. These apps contain:
- Production: ProductionOrder, Bin, BinHistory, Batch, BatchItem models with 869 lines of view logic
- Purchasing: PurchaseRequest, PurchaseOrder, Receiving models with 1084 lines of view logic
ideas.proposedChange:
Create comprehensive test files:
- apps/production/tests.py (model tests for ProductionOrder, Bin, Batch)
- apps/production/test_views.py (view tests for CRUD operations, status transitions)
- apps/purchasing/tests.py (model tests for PurchaseRequest, PurchaseOrder, Receiving)
- apps/purchasing/test_views.py (view tests for request/order workflow)
ideas.codeExample:
# apps/production/tests.py (following existing patterns from apps/inventory/tests.py)
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse
from apps.production.models import ProductionOrder, Batch
from apps.materials.models import Material
from apps.accounts.models import CustomUser

class ProductionOrderModelTests(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.user = CustomUser.objects.create_user(...)
        self.material = Material.objects.create(...)
    
    def test_order_number_auto_generated(self):
        order = ProductionOrder.objects.create(
            material=self.material,
            planned_quantity=100
        )
        self.assertTrue(order.order_number.startswith('OP'))
    
    def test_completion_percentage(self):
        order = ProductionOrder.objects.create(
            material=self.material,
            planned_quantity=100,
            produced_quantity=50
        )
        self.assertEqual(order.completion_percentage, 50)
ideas.bestPractice: All business-critical functionality should have unit tests. Django's TestCase class provides database transactions that are rolled back after each test.

ideas.title: Extract duplicated list view pagination/filtering into reusable mixin or utility
ideas.description: The codebase contains 14+ list views that all follow the same pattern: get filters from request.GET, apply filters to queryset, paginate results, and render template. This pattern is duplicated across inventory, purchasing, production, materials, and labels apps.
ideas.rationale: Code duplication leads to inconsistencies when fixes are applied unevenly and increases maintenance burden. A reusable mixin or utility function would ensure consistent behavior, reduce boilerplate, and make adding new list views faster and less error-prone.
ideas.currentState:
Each list view manually implements:
1. Extract search/filter params from request.GET
2. Build queryset with select_related/prefetch_related
3. Apply search filter with Q objects
4. Apply additional filters
5. Create Paginator with hardcoded page size (20-50)
6. Get paginated page
7. Build context dict
8. Render template

This pattern appears in: stock_list, movements_list, warehouse_list, reservations_list, inventory_count_list, request_list, order_list, receiving_list, production_order_list, bin_list, batch_list, material_list, supplier_list, template_list, printer_list, print_job_list
ideas.proposedChange:
Create a reusable ListView mixin in apps/core/views.py:
1. BaseListView class that handles pagination, search, and common filter patterns
2. FilterMixin for declaring filterable fields
3. SearchMixin for Q-object based search

Alternatively, use Django's built-in class-based ListView with custom mixins for the filtering logic.
ideas.bestPractice: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) - extract common patterns into reusable components. Django class-based views and mixins are designed for exactly this use case.
prerequisites: Good test coverage on existing list views before refactoring

ideas.title: Add Python linting and code quality configuration
ideas.description: The project has no linting configuration files (flake8, pylint, mypy). Without automated code quality checks, inconsistent coding styles, unused imports, and type errors can accumulate over time.
ideas.rationale: Linting tools catch common bugs, enforce consistent code style, and improve code readability. They are especially valuable in team environments and CI/CD pipelines. The project already uses pyproject.toml which can host most linting configuration.
ideas.currentState: No linting tools configured. pyproject.toml only has basic project metadata and dependencies. No .flake8, .pylintrc, setup.cfg, or mypy.ini files exist.
ideas.proposedChange:
Add linting configuration to pyproject.toml and set up pre-commit hooks:
1. Add ruff (modern, fast Python linter) configuration to pyproject.toml
2. Configure basic rules: unused imports, line length, import sorting
3. Add Django-specific rules
4. Optionally add mypy for gradual type checking
5. Set up pre-commit hooks for automatic linting
ideas.codeExample:
# Add to pyproject.toml
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",  # pycodestyle errors
    "W",  # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",  # pyflakes
    "I",  # isort
    "B",  # flake8-bugbear
    "C4", # flake8-comprehensions
    "DJ", # flake8-django
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line too long (handled by formatter)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["apps", "config"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.10"
plugins = ["mypy_django_plugin.main"]
ignore_missing_imports = true
strict_optional = true

# requirements-dev.txt addition
ruff>=0.1.0
mypy>=1.0.0
django-stubs>=4.0.0
pre-commit>=3.0.0
ideas.bestPractice: Every Python project should have automated code quality checks. Ruff is the modern choice - it's faster than flake8/isort/black combined and supports Django-specific rules.
